# bugs #2970: sdas opens the .rel file in text mode again since r16921, which removes the fix of r12963

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2970/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: judged by reading, against r17192
- Recommended action: Decide whether r16921 changed the mode on purpose. If not, apply the patch, which has no test and was not run on Windows.
- Patch: [bugs-2970.patch](../../patches/bugs-2970.patch), commit [`27cd066b4`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/27cd066b410351fa4e009bdf3c1635728fbd9675). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The fix for this ticket is not in effect in r17176. Since
[r12963](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/12963/), `afile` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asmain.c` opened
the files that the assembler writes with the mode `"wb"`. Since
[r16921](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/16921/) the mode for the write code 1 is `"w"`.
`main` in the same file passes the code 1 for the `.lst`, `.rel`, and `.sym` files. No code in
`sdas` selects binary mode in another way. By the code, sdas on a Windows host writes these files
with CRLF line endings again. The ticket has the status pending-fixed.

This was read in the source. No Windows host was available, and sdas was not run on Windows.

Two parts were run on a Linux host with r17176 for mcs51. The build in the ticket, with `--debug`,
`sdar`, and two libraries, links without a message. After the line endings in the `.rel` files of
the four library members were changed to CRLF, `sdar` printed the message of the ticket for each
file, and the linker reported `_bar`, `_bat`, and `_mat` as undefined. These are the symptoms in
the ticket. The same build without `--debug` links without a message with CRLF files.

## Cause

`asxxxx_is_rel` in `support/sdbinutils/bfd/asxxxx.c` rejects the files. With `--debug` the `.rel`
file starts with a `;!FILE` line. `asxxxx_skip_line` stops at the `\r` of that line, and
`asxxxx_get_eol` accepts the `\r` and does not read the `\n` after it. `asxxxx_is_rel` then reads
the `\n` as the first character of the format line and reports it, which is the `\012` in the
message. A file without the `;!FILE` line does not reach this code, so the defect needs `--debug`.

r16921 has the log message "More small changes from upstream asxxxx". In `afile`, the line of sdas
with `"wb"` and the comment from r12963 were replaced by a line with `"w"`. In the same revision
the first parameter of `afile` got a new name and `afilex` got a third parameter. Neither the log
message nor the ChangeLog entry mentions the mode.

## Fix

`afile` opens the write code 1 with `"wb"` again. The line and its comment are between the markers
`sdas specific` and `end sdas specific`, which `asmain.c` has around its other code that is
particular to sdas.

## Decision

The patch is right only if the mode change in r16921 was not intended. By the code, the defect is
gone with any one of three changes. Only the first was built, and none was run on a Windows host.

- The patch. `afile` differs in one line from the code merged in r16921, and the line can be lost
  again in a later merge. On a Windows host the `.lst`, `.rel`, and `.sym` files get LF line
  endings, as from r12963 to r16920.
- `main` passes the write code 3 for the three files. `afile` has `"wb"` for that code and stays
  as merged, and `afilex` does not use the code. Three calls in `main` differ then. The call for
  the `.rel` file is between sdas markers already.
- `asxxxx_is_rel` reads a `\n` after the `\r` of the `;!FILE` line. The files keep CRLF line
  endings on a Windows host. No other reader of the `.rel` file was examined for CRLF.

## Verification

The patch has no test. The modes `"w"` and `"wb"` do not differ on a POSIX host, so a test on
Linux cannot fail without the patch. The patch was not built or run on a Windows host. On Linux,
with this patch and the patches for local 0009 and bug #3703, the regression suite for
mcs51-small, stm8, and ucz80 and the diagnostics suite for mcs51 have no failure.
